approved: Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill temporarily raises the cap on farm assets and adds a two-part payment top-up for eligible recipients of the Farm Household Allowance.
The top-up and the higher asset limit would apply only until mid-2019, with the exact start date for the new asset ceiling set by ministerial rule.
Under the current rules, the farm asset limit is $2.635 million, and the bill would raise it to $5 million until 30 June 2019.
The bill increases the farm assets limit from $2.635 million to $5 million.
The bill introduces a two-part payment supplement for qualifying Farm Household Allowance recipients.
The increased asset limit and the supplement are temporary, ending by 30 June 2019.
Farmers and their partners who receive the Farm Household Allowance.

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2018-08-22.12.2) moved by Hunter MP [Joel Fitzgibbon](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/hunter/joel_fitzgibbon) (Labor), which means it failed. The amendment was to the usual second reading motion - that the bill be [read a second time](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) - which is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > >> *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House calls on the Turnbull Government to:* >> >>> *(1) allow eligible farmers the option of receiving the Farm Household Allowance supplement in a single $12,000 up-front payment; and* >>> >>> *(2) prioritise the resurrection of the COAG process it dismantled in 2013, in order to restore progress on the development of the National Drought Policy Reform Program."*

The Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018 was moved, proposing a temporary increase to the net farm assets threshold for the Farm Household Allowance (FHA) to $5 million (effective 1 November 2018 to 30 June 2019) and introducing automatic lump-sum supplement payments of $3,000 per person for couples and $3,600 for singles (with a maximum of $7,200 for singles) between 1 September 2018 and 1 July 2019. The bill also includes an additional $5 million for the Rural Financial Counselling Service and is part of a $576 million government commitment to drought-affected farmers, pending an independent review of the FHA program to be completed in the first half of 2019.

The speaker criticised the government's drought and dairy crisis responses as too late and inadequate, noting that up to 10 farming families in Braddon still receive Farm Household Allowance from the 2016 dairy crisis, and called for Labor's alternative policies: restoring the COAG drought reform process, developing an agricultural climate response plan, establishing a $20 million regional economic development fund, and improving Farm Household Allowance processing.

The speaker supported the Farm Household Support Amendment Bill 2018, which expands the farm household allowance by lifting asset tests from $2.55 million to $5 million and provides two lump sum payments of up to $3,600 each, while also calling for government action on climate change, energy costs, and bank lending practices, and noting plans to re-table the Banking Amendment (Rural Finance Reform) Bill 2018.

The speaker supported the Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018, citing expanded eligibility with the asset test threshold raised to $5 million, additional $12,000 grants, and streamlined application processes. He also welcomed drought relief measures including a drought coordinator, tax deductions for fodder storage, low-interest loans up to $2 million, $23.7 million for artesian bore capping, $72 million for water infrastructure, and $1 million council grants, while urging faster delivery of grain, fodder, and rural financial counsellors to central west New South Wales.

The speaker supported the Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018, which extends support from three to four years and raises the farm asset limit from $2.635 million to $5 million. They also criticised the government for cutting 2,500 Centrelink staff, noting that two-thirds of eligible farmers (15,000) have not accessed the allowance due to complex forms and long wait times, and announced Labor's plan to add 1,200 permanent staff and 100 community response officers.

The government should have supported the opposition's amendment for a $12,000 single upfront payment to farmers and the rebuilding of the COAG process for a National Drought Policy Reform Program. The government was also criticised for failing on drought policy, Centrelink’s complex paperwork and processing delays, and for allegedly allocating drought funding to councils in a partisan manner.

The member supported the Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018, highlighting the extra $12,000 per couple, additional funding for the Rural Financial Counselling Service, mental health support, and one-year accelerated depreciation for hay, grain storage, fencing and water. He praised the Prime Minister and senior ministers for their drought response, and criticised opposition contributions as patronising while defending farmers as professional and adapting to climate change.

The speaker supported the Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018, arguing for an increased farm asset threshold and a $6,000 lump sum payment per couple to help drought-affected NSW farmers, and highlighted the Rural Financial Counselling Service and the donation of approximately 20 road trains of hay from Western Australia.

The speaker announced the Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018, which increases the farm assets threshold to a net $5 million until 30 June 2019 and pays a supplement of up to $12,000 per household to eligible Farm Household Allowance recipients. The speaker also urged farmers to call the Rural Financial Counselling Service on 1800686175 or the family assistance hotline on 132316, and noted that $5 million has been allocated for face-to-face counselling, while highlighting a request to supermarket CEOs for a 20-cent price increase on milk to support dairy farmers.

The bill increases the net farm assets threshold to $5 million until 30 June 2019 and provides a supplement of up to $12,000 for couples and $7,200 for single recipients of the Farm Household Allowance.

The government moved an amendment to the Farm Household Support Amendment (Temporary Measures) Bill 2018 to bring forward the increase in the farm assets threshold to $5 million from 1 November 2018 to 1 September 2018, allowing farmers with net farm assets up to $5 million to lodge applications from that date with payments backdated to lodgement.
